independence_declaration.statement: I am domain-reviewer, run T-DG1-REV-DOM-R8. I authored no implementation, register text or decision in the DG1 scope. I also did not author the round-8 repair: the F-DG1-128 lint change is backend-workflow-engineer work (T-DG1-BE9), and D-054 was written by the orchestrator. I formed this verdict before reading any other reviewer's round-8 record, and none was visible to me. The earlier review material I used was my own round-7 domain-reviewer record and harness scripts (re-used here as round-8 copies), the round-7 code-security F-DG1-128 findings sidecar (to see the claim's basis), and the findings.json status entries for the findings my assignment names. I grant no business, Finance or IT approval. Product gate G6 is not engineering gate DG7.

Check that HEAD differs from the freeze commit only by candidate-excluded metadata, and that a full disposable clone at 11bc4c4 recomputes the same id with an identical lockfile.

checks_run.actual: Every computation gives sha256:e27eaf5fb5ada8640c4463b8e3c9d5f64e5aa629fa78b49cfd2861bdc7544876 (390 files), and --diff reports matches=true with none added, removed or changed. checks_run.procedure: Check that the F-DG1-128 fix does not over-reach, using a reviewer-authored probe on the candidate's own testkit. The round-7 testkit (a6bdea0) is copied in as zz-r7.testkit.ts for a differential. (a) 47 legitimate specifiers stay allowed: the real tree's bare specifiers (collected with the lint's own importsOf), common node: built-ins, the @mth packages and every api dependency. (b) Specifier differential over 164 specifiers: every builtinModules entry, bare and node:, plus the prefix-only modules. (c) process-member differential over all 109 own and prototype keys of the live process object, each as `process.<m>`; ordinary members stay clean. (d) 15 import and call forms of node:test and process.execve. (e) The real module tree has 0 violations.
checks_run.command: git show a6bdea0:apps/api/src/architecture.testkit.ts > apps/api/src/zz-r7.testkit.ts; cp 03-f128-overreach-probe.test.ts apps/api/src/zz-dom8-probe.test.ts; npx vitest run --project unit-node --reporter=verbose apps/api/src/zz-dom8-probe.test.ts; rm both probe files
checks_run.environment: Disposable clone at 11bc4c4, node v22.22.2. The probe files are removed afterwards and git status is clean.
checks_run.expected: No legitimate specifier is rejected. The only specifier verdict change from round 7 is node:test; bare `test` was already rejected because a bare non-node: specifier must be a declared dependency. The only newly flagged process member is execve. Every node:test and execve form is caught, and the real tree has 0 violations.
checks_run.actual: (a) 0 of 47 rejected. (b) The only verdict change across 164 specifiers is 'node:test: r7=true r8=false'. (c) Across 109 members, only ["execve"] is newly flagged. _linkedBinding, binding, constructor, dlopen and getBuiltinModule were flagged in both versions, and env, cwd, hrtime, nextTick, platform, version, pid, uptime, memoryUsage, on, emitWarning and exitCode stay clean. (d) 0 of 15 forms missed. (e) 0 violations. 5/5 passed, exit 0. Run 1 is kept in *.run1-probe-bug.out.txt: it took its corpus from builtinModules alone, which on Node 22 omits the prefix-only node:test, node:sqlite and node:sea, so (b) wrongly saw no change. That was a probe bug, not a candidate defect, and run 2 adds those modules explicitly.

checks_run.procedure: Read the testkit header and D-054, and check that the exhaustive-enumeration claim honestly describes a defence-in-depth lint. The text must not claim a runtime security boundary, must name the residuals, and must state its validation scope correctly. Compare the 'pinned Node version (22.x)' statement with the repository's actual runtime pins: .nvmrc, engines, the production Dockerfile image, the CI matrix and ADR-0001. Before raising anything, check it against the stated residual (c).
checks_run.command: git diff a6bdea0 11bc4c4 -- apps/api/src/architecture.testkit.ts; grep '| D-054 |' docs/delivery/decisions.md; grep -n 'NOT a runtime security boundary' apps/api/src/architecture.testkit.ts; cat .nvmrc; grep '"node"' package.json; grep '^ARG NODE_IMAGE' deploy/docker/Dockerfile; grep 'node: \[' deploy/ci/ci.yml; sed -n 19,24p docs/architecture/adr/ADR-0001-runtime-language-package-manager.md; ls -d /opt/node2*
checks_run.environment: Candidate tree at 11bc4c4 content (HEAD 6cb3813, identical candidate)
checks_run.expected: The claim is honest. It is a static defence-in-depth lint and not a runtime boundary, it is not a user-facing change, and its exhaustiveness is stated for the runtime it was validated on.
checks_run.actual: Mostly honest. The header keeps 'it is NOT a runtime security boundary', residuals (a), (b) and (c) are named, wasi/WebAssembly and the deferred default-deny allow-list are disclosed, and nothing user-facing changed. One misstatement: the claim calls 22.x 'the PINNED Node version'. In fact .nvmrc is 24, the production image is node:24-bookworm-slim@sha256:0e0ff40c…, and ADR-0001 sets the target runtime to Node 24 LTS with 22.18+ only as the floor. The validating sweep ran on 22.22.2 only, and residual (c) covers only 'a LATER Node version', not the current target. I could not sweep Node 24: the sandbox has no Node 24 binary and no network. Raised as Low and not mandatory (F-DG1-010): it is documentation accuracy, not a demonstrated route.

summary: PASS with one new Low, non-mandatory finding (F-DG1-010). Candidate e27eaf5f is confirmed: freeze commit 11bc4c4, and HEAD 6cb3813 adds only metadata. Since round 7 only the module lint and its self-test changed, and both are excluded from the build. There is no product, runtime, API, data-model, register or i18n change. The F-DG1-128 fix does not over-reach. Across 164 specifiers (every builtinModules entry plus the prefix-only modules) the only verdict change is node:test. Across all 109 process members the only newly flagged member is execve. All 47 legitimate specifiers stay allowed, and the real module tree has 0 violations. There is no domain regression: 273/273 unit tests, 2 x 200/200 integration runs with no leftovers, and 108/108 live checks in ar and en. These cover the G6 closure refused with 422, scoped access, cursor binding, identity routes, provisional branding, Unknown shown instead of zero, and the localized audit. All 12 round-7 domain closures still hold. The 8 assigned rows are IMPLEMENTED with all evidence present, and no P1-increment row is over-claimed. Finding: D-054 and the testkit call 22.x 'the PINNED Node version' and declare the enumeration exhaustive for it. But the repository's target runtime is Node 24 (ADR-0001, .nvmrc, the digest-pinned production image), and residual (c) covers only later versions. The exhaustiveness claim is therefore validated on the floor/sandbox version, not on the shipped runtime. This is documentation accuracy only. I demonstrated no route, and I could not sweep Node 24 here because the sandbox has no Node 24 binary and no network.
